why: Six float comparisons branch with `fcomp`/`fcompp; fnstsw ax; test ah, 5; jp` (0x100CFE52, 0x100CFE80, 0x100CFEB0, 0x100CFEC3, 0x100CFEDB, 0x100CFEF0). After FCOM, C0 (AH bit 0x01) is set for less, C3 for equal, and C0, C2 and C3 for unordered; `test ah, 5` keeps C0|C2, and PF is set for 0 (greater, equal) and for 5 (unordered), clear for 1 (less), so the jump is taken exactly when !(ST0 < src): including NaN. Hex-Rays wrote each as `ST0 >= src`, which is false for NaN, so with a NaN operand the reconstruction took the other branch. Each is written !(ST0 < src), with the operands in the original's order.
evidence: Live gate on all four same-build dumps (runs/r5/liveall_*): FAIL in 1 of 100 trials, memory differs at a3: original stores 0xFFFBFFB9 at 0x100CFECF, reconstruction 0x7FFC01B9 (line `*(float *)(a3 + 4) = v37;`), a NaN in the input taking the other branch. Disassembly 0x100CFE48..0x100CFEFC; Intel SDM FCOM condition codes.
